question: Part ___________________ of the Constitution of India deals with the Union Executive.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Part V**__ of the Constitution of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Part V** of the Constitution of India deals with the Union Executive.
 
• It includes Articles **52 to 78**.
 
• The Union Executive consists of the **President, the Vice-President, the Prime Minister, the Council of Ministers, and the Attorney General of India**.
 
• The President of India is the **head of the state** and the **supreme commander of the armed forces**.
 
• The executive power of the Union is vested in the President and is exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President of India**:

 
 
• The President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.
 
• The President holds office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters his office.
 
• The President can be impeached for violation of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Vice-President of India**:
 
 
• The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both houses of Parliament.
 
• He acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• In the event of the death or resignation of the President, the Vice-President discharges the functions of the President.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister of India**:
 
 
• The Prime Minister is appointed by the President and is the head of the government.
 
• He advises the President in the exercise of his functions.
 
• The Prime Minister heads the Council of Ministers, which is the real executive authority.
 
 
 
• **Attorney General of India**:
 
 
• The Attorney General is the highest law officer in the country.
 
• He is appointed by the President and holds office during the pleasure of the President.
 
• He has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both houses of Parliament but without a right to vote.
